children: Wall Street
the week mixed as a sharp spike in volatility reflected fresh tech struggles, while investors continued to digest hotter-than-expected CPI data and the latest bank earnings.
State Street Financial Sel Sec SPDR ETF
advanced 1.44% from the prior week to close at $55.52.
Among megacap financial stocks, Toronto-Dominion Bank
was a notable gainer, adding 4.60% week-over-week to $120.39.
TD Bank was among the nine largest U.S. banks
the so-called "debanking" activity, according to the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency's recent report.
The stock lost 0.27% on the day, but was rising for the remainder of the week.
Mastercard
(+4.80% W/W to $617.42) and Visa
(+4.45% W/W to $402.61) were the other major gainers. The two stocks have been gaining since the launch of Open USD
stablecoin last month.
Bank of America
led the decliners, having posted its worst day since April 2025 on Wednesday. The stock fell 5.69% week-over-week to $51.23.
The stock plunged after the U.S. Department of the Treasury
over $1.21B in penalties against the lender over anti-money laundering and sanctions laws violations. The regulatory fine impacted the bank's third-quarter profit.
Morgan Stanley's
Q3 earnings exceeded expectations despite a weakness in fixed income and investment management. However, the stock underperformed with a 4.97% decline to $180.57.
Citigroup
followed with a 4.15% decrease to $124.26. Q3 earnings beat analyst estimates but saw sequential declines across investment banking, trading, and firm-wide profitability.
The KBW Nasdaq Bank Index
underperformed the broader markets, with investors split on how to read Q3 bank earnings, according to a report by S&P Global Market Intelligence.

"One camp sees positive net interest income outlooks and strong returns and capital and consumer spend. The other sees rising deposits costs and [accumulated other comprehensive income] eating buybacks and concerns on lending standards and credit sustainability," said Truist Securities analyst Brian Foran.
Among largecap stocks, TransUnion
topped the advancers with a 13.13% addition to $74.08. The week saw TransUnion strike a deal with Bankrate to power more personalized credit offers for millions of consumers.
Additionally, a general strength was seen across the broader credit reporting sector.
IREN
(-23.30% W/W to $26.99) was the biggest loser despite the crypto miner-turned-AI server agreeing on a multiyear cloud deal with Anthropic.
The week saw most neocloud stocks fall after a report by Gartner predicted 80% of neoclouds will cease independent operations by 2030 if AI infrastructure spending continues at its breakneck speed.
Pershing Square
was the next on the list, retreating 18.52% to $44.48. The stock was downgraded at Citi and BofA Securities.
MARA Holdings
(-21.97% W/W to $7.53), Galaxy Digital
(-20.61% W/W to $16.14), and CleanSpark
(-19.96% W/W to $8.40) were among the top midcap decliners.
For the winners, insurance stocks RLI
(+9.62% W/W to $61.07), Kinsale Capital
(+8.39% W/W to $365.24), Slide Insurance
(+7.68% W/W to $27.07), and Hagerty
(+7.67% W/W to $15.30). The sector was trading higher on the back of above-expected earnings posted by Travelers
and Marsh
American Coastal Insurance
(+8.58% W/W to $7.34), Bit Digital
(-25.60% W/W to $0.96), and Bitgo Holdings
(-19.78% W/W to $5.88) were the notable smallcap movers.

title: Insurance stocks, TransUnion among winners; Banks, IREN in losers: week's financials wrap
